title: Regular local rings characterized by canonical symmetric cotangent multiplication
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with residue field $k=R/\mathfrak n$ and cotangent vector space $V=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. Put $e=\dim_k V$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Let $\operatorname{Sym}_k(V)$ be the symmetric algebra, the quotient of the tensor algebra by the relations $v\otimes w-w\otimes v$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], and let $\operatorname{Sym}^q_k(V)$ be its degree-$q$ subspace spanned by products of $q$ vectors [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Multiplication of representatives defines canonical $k$-linear maps
$$\mu_{R,q}:\operatorname{Sym}^q_k(V)\longrightarrow\mathfrak n^q/\mathfrak n^{q+1},\qquad
\bar a_1\cdots\bar a_q\longmapsto a_1\cdots a_q\bmod\mathfrak n^{q+1}\quad(q\geq1),$$
where $a_i\in\mathfrak n$ represents $\bar a_i\in V$. Together with $\mu_{R,0}=\mathrm{id}_k$ these define the canonical graded $k$-algebra map from $\operatorname{Sym}_k(V)$ to $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}R$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. The ring $R$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] if and only if $\mu_{R,q}$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq1$. Whenever these equivalent conditions hold, $\dim R=e$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: 13.2(a), printed p.254 (canonical Sym_k(n/n^2) to gr(R) criterion); 13.2 introductory paragraph and (b). Supporting Stacks Project algebra.tex Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded) and Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension).

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure], $G$ is a commutative $k$-algebra and its degree-one inclusion $V\to G$ is $k$-linear. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] to obtain $\mu:\operatorname{Sym}_k(V)\to G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], its degree-$q$ source is spanned by products of $q$ vectors. Multiplication in $G$ sends such a product to the class of the product of representatives, exactly the displayed $\mu_{R,q}$. Changing one representative by $b\in\mathfrak n^2$ changes that product by an element of $\mathfrak n^{q+1}$; changing a scalar lift by an element of $\mathfrak n$ does the same. Thus the formula is well defined, $k$-linear, degree preserving, and the degree-zero map is the identity.

source.place: Tag 061N (equation-quasi-regular), multiplication formula; Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), symmetric universal map. Milne 13.2(a), printed p.254, canonical map.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $e$ is finite. Choose a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_e$ of $V$ and lifts $a_i\in\mathfrak n$. Noetherianity makes $\mathfrak n$ finitely generated, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to the module $\mathfrak n$ with $\mathfrak n\mathfrak n=\mathfrak n^2$, shows that the $a_i$ generate it. Identifying $V$ with $k^{\oplus e}$ via this basis, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] gives $\beta:\operatorname{Sym}_k(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}P=k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$, $v_i\mapsto T_i$. This is graded: products of $q$ vectors map to degree-$q$ polynomials, and every degree-$q$ monomial maps back to a product of $q$ basis vectors. Put $\theta=\mu\beta^{-1}$. Its degree-$q$ map is onto, since [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge] says that products of the $a_i$ span $G_q$. It is the identity in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), first two proof sentences; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), generators; Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), finite free symmetric algebra.

proof.text: First dispose of $e=0$. Step 2 says that the empty list generates $\mathfrak n$, hence $\mathfrak n=0$. Therefore $R=k$ is a field, $G_0=k$, and $G_q=0$ for $q>0$; the same holds for $\operatorname{Sym}_k(0)$. Every positive-degree map is an isomorphism. The only prime of a field is $(0)$, so $\dim R=0$, and the empty generating list makes $R$ regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This proves both directions and the dimension assertion when $e=0$. Henceforth $e\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local), dimension-zero case of Tag 00NO; explicit empty-variable case.

proof.text: Suppose $R$ is regular. Then [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim R=e$. Let $I=\ker\theta\subset P$. Since $\theta$ respects degrees, if a finite sum of homogeneous polynomials lies in $I$, each summand does, by uniqueness of components in $G$. Thus $I$ is homogeneous, and it is proper because $\theta|_k=\mathrm{id}_k$. In each degree, $P_q/(I\cap P_q)\to G_q$ is a linear bijection: surjectivity is step 2 and its kernel is exactly $I\cap P_q$. If $I\ne0$, [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-cumulative-growth] supplies a nonzero eventual polynomial $Q_I$ of degree less than $e$ for $\sum_{q<n}\dim_kG_q$. By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge] that sum is $H_R(n)=\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak n^n)$, whereas [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] gives an eventual polynomial $Q_R$ of degree $\dim R=e$ for the same function. They agree at every sufficiently large integer, so [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] over $\mathbf Q$ gives $Q_I=Q_R$, a contradiction. Therefore $I=0$. Each $\theta_q$ is bijective and, through $\beta$, so is each canonical $\mu_{R,q}$.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), Hilbert-function contradiction, using Tag 00K3 (lemma-quotient-smaller-d) and Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension).

proof.text:
Conversely assume every $\mu_{R,q}$, $q\geq1$, is an isomorphism. Through $\beta$ and the identity in degree zero, $G_q$ has the monomial basis of the degree-$q$ part of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge], $H_R(n)$ is therefore the number of tuples $\alpha\in\mathbf N^e$ with $|\alpha|<n$. This number is $\binom{n+e-1}{e}$: partition into tuples with first coordinate zero and positive to obtain $c(e,n)=c(e-1,n)+c(e,n-1)$, with $c(0,n)=1$ for $n\geq1$ and $c(e,1)=1$; Pascal's identity gives the formula by induction. Thus for all $n\geq1$,
$$H_R(n)=B_e(n),\qquad B_e(X)=\frac{X(X+1)\cdots(X+e-1)}{e!},$$
a polynomial over $\mathbf Q$ of degree $e$ and leading coefficient $1/e!$. The eventual polynomial $Q_R$ of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] agrees with $B_e$ at infinitely many rational integers; [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] gives equality. Consequently $\dim R=\deg Q_R=e$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] implies that $R$ is regular. Together with steps 3 and 4 this proves the equivalence and the stated dimension in every case.
